Get the estimates of a fitted profile or class model as starting values for another fit

Source: R/accessors.R
starting_values.Rd

starting_values() returns the parameter estimates of a fitted profile or class model in the form multilpa() accepts as start, so that a second fit begins from the first one's solution. The measurement parameters can be taken alone, for a refit that estimates the class probabilities anew. Starting values are where the estimation begins, not constraints: to hold parameters fixed, use the fixed argument of the fitting function.

Usage

starting_values(
  x,
  covariance = c("auto", "drop", "keep"),
  what = c("all", "measurement")
)

Arguments

x

The source of the values, one of:

  • a fit from lpa(), lca(), multilpa() or multilca() without membership covariates;

  • a list with profile_probabilities, group_probabilities and the measurement blocks the model uses: means with variances or covariances for continuous indicators, response_probabilities for categorical ones (a model with only categorical indicators needs no means). Other elements are ignored.

A fit with membership covariates and a model of another family carry no such blocks and raise latents_bad_start, as does a transition fit from lta(), which takes no start.

covariance

How the within-profile covariances are returned:

  • "auto" (default): covariances when x has them (a fit with a full covariance structure), otherwise variances;

  • "drop": always variances, the diagonal form;

  • "keep": covariances, raising latents_bad_start when x has none.

what

Which blocks to return:

  • "all" (default): the measurement blocks and the mixing blocks (profile_probabilities and group_probabilities);

  • "measurement": the measurement blocks only. The mixing blocks are sized for the model that produced them, so leave them out for a refit with another number of group classes, together with fixed in multilpa().

Value

An object of class multilpa_start: the list that multilpa() accepts as start, which can be passed on as it is. Its elements:

  • means: a matrix, profiles by continuous indicators;

  • variances: a matrix of the same shape; or, when covariances are returned, covariances in its place: an array, indicators by indicators by profiles;

  • profile_probabilities: a matrix, group classes by profiles, and group_probabilities: a vector with one value per group class. Both are left out under what = "measurement";

  • response_probabilities: for a model with categorical indicators, a list with one matrix per indicator, profiles by categories.

The Gaussian blocks are unnamed and matched by position. response_probabilities keeps the indicator and category names, and multilpa() matches its blocks by them.

Printing the object summarises the blocks. as.data.frame() returns the means and variances as a table, one row per profile and indicator, and get_results() the tables "profiles", "responses", "profile_probabilities" and "covariances".

Conditions raised:

  • latents_bad_start: x lacks a block that is needed, is a transition fit, or has no covariances under covariance = "keep". multilpa() raises the same class for a start whose categorical indicators or categories do not match the model;

  • latents_unsupported_noise: x is a fit with a noise component;

  • latents_bad_argument: x is not a list.

Details

This is a utility for controlled refitting. starting_values() checks that the blocks it needs are present; the fitting function checks their dimensions and values.

See also

get_results() for the values as tidy tables; fit_staged() for two-stage estimation with fixed measurement parameters.

Examples

set.seed(7)
example_data <- data.frame(
  school = rep(seq_len(12), each = 10),
  score_a = rnorm(120), score_b = rnorm(120)
)
fit <- multilpa(example_data, c("score_a", "score_b"), "school",
                n_profiles = 2, n_group_classes = 1, n_starts = 2, seed = 1)
starting_values(fit)
#> Starting values: 2 profile(s), 2 continuous indicator(s)
#> Residual covariance: diagonal
#> Categorical indicators: 0
#> Mixing blocks: 1 group class(es)
#> Pass this to multilpa(start = ) as it is.
as.data.frame(starting_values(fit))
#>   profile indicator        mean  variance standard_deviation
#> 1       1         1  0.31636435 0.7483133          0.8650510
#> 2       1         2 -0.05291897 0.9149761          0.9565438
#> 3       2         1 -1.11359384 0.1018719          0.3191738
#> 4       2         2  0.79093314 0.2857893          0.5345926
refit <- multilpa(example_data, c("score_a", "score_b"), "school",
                  n_profiles = 2, n_group_classes = 1, n_starts = 1,
                  start = starting_values(fit))
logLik(refit)
#> 'log Lik.' -323.0197 (df=9)
